title: Nature's giants
paragraphs: When thinking of giant animals, dinosaurs might be the first creatures you think of. But before the dinosaurs became extinct, and before the first ever humans existed, there was megafauna. In zoology, this means large animals.

One of the largest known mammals to have ever walked the Earth is the Paraceratherium – picture a gigantic hornless rhino, and you'll have a rough idea of what they looked like. They lived around 25 million years ago and were most common in areas of the world that are now part of Asia, such as China, India and Kazakhstan. From excavated fossils, these creatures are estimated to have been almost six metres tall – that's the height of two buses on top of each other!

And it's not just land enormous creatures lived on – they were in the skies and oceans too. The Argentavis is the largest flying bird to have been discovered. It lived until around six million years ago and had a wingspan of seven metres, over twice the size of the Andean condor, which is one of the largest birds on Earth today. And we can't forget the giant shark that roamed the oceans, megalodon. Imagine swimming in the sea and coming across an 18-metre-long shark! Don't worry. They died out around 2.6 million years ago.

So, why were pre-historic animals so huge? There are a number of reasons. One is that, in the past, resources were more plentiful, so species were able to grow larger because they could eat more. Scientists also believe that during certain periods of history, such as in the Carboniferous period, there were higher oxygen levels on Earth. At this time, some insects grew to the size of cars because of better oxygen delivery in their tracheal system, the network of tubes that enable insects to breathe.
Can you picture animals being so huge today?

vocabulary.entry: **extinct** /ɪkˈstɪŋkt/ adj. 灭绝的，绝种的（书面语）
vocabulary.example: Many species of animals are now at risk of becoming extinct.
vocabulary.translation: 许多动物物种现在面临灭绝的风险。

vocabulary.entry: **megafauna** /ˈmeɡəfɔːnə/ n. 巨型动物群（专业术语，书面语）
vocabulary.example: The study of megafauna helps us understand prehistoric ecosystems.
vocabulary.translation: 对巨型动物群的研究有助于我们理解史前生态系统。

vocabulary.entry: **zoology** /zuˈɒlədʒi/ n. 动物学（专业术语，书面语）
vocabulary.example: Zoology is the scientific study of animals.
vocabulary.translation: 动物学是对动物的科学研究。

vocabulary.entry: **mammal** /ˈmæml/ n. 哺乳动物（专业术语）
vocabulary.example: Humans, dogs, and whales are all mammals.
vocabulary.translation: 人类、狗和鲸鱼都是哺乳动物。

vocabulary.entry: **Paraceratherium** /ˌpærəsərəˈθɪəriəm/ n. 副巨犀（古生物属名，专有名词）
vocabulary.example: Paraceratherium is one of the largest land mammals ever discovered.
vocabulary.translation: 副巨犀是有史以来发现的最大的陆生哺乳动物之一。

vocabulary.entry: **gigantic** /dʒaɪˈɡæntɪk/ adj. 巨大的，庞大的（书面语）
vocabulary.example: The new shopping centre is gigantic.
vocabulary.translation: 新购物中心规模巨大。

vocabulary.entry: **hornless** /ˈhɔːnləs/ adj. 无角的
vocabulary.example: The hornless rhino looked very different from modern rhinos.
vocabulary.translation: 无角犀牛看起来与现代犀牛非常不同。

vocabulary.entry: **rhino** /ˈraɪnəʊ/ n. 犀牛（口语，rhinoceros的缩写）
vocabulary.example: The rhino charged at the vehicle.
vocabulary.translation: 犀牛冲向车辆。

vocabulary.entry: **excavate** /ˈekskəveɪt/ v. 挖掘，发掘（书面语）
vocabulary.example: Archaeologists excavated the ancient city.
vocabulary.translation: 考古学家挖掘了这座古城。

vocabulary.entry: **fossil** /ˈfɒsl/ n. 化石
vocabulary.example: The fossil of a dinosaur was found in the desert.
vocabulary.translation: 在沙漠中发现了一具恐龙化石。

vocabulary.entry: **estimate** /ˈestɪmeɪt/ v. 估计，估算
vocabulary.example: We estimate the journey will take two hours.
vocabulary.translation: 我们估计这段路程需要两小时。

vocabulary.entry: **wingspan** /ˈwɪŋspæn/ n. 翼展（专业术语）
vocabulary.example: The eagle has a wingspan of over two metres.
vocabulary.translation: 这只鹰的翼展超过两米。

vocabulary.entry: **Andean condor** /ænˈdiːən ˈkɒndɔː(r)/ n. 安第斯神鹰（专有名词）
vocabulary.example: The Andean condor is one of the largest flying birds in the world.
vocabulary.translation: 安第斯神鹰是世界上最大的飞鸟之一。

vocabulary.entry: **roam** /rəʊm/ v. 漫游，游荡（书面语）
vocabulary.example: Wild horses roam freely across the plains.
vocabulary.translation: 野马在平原上自由漫游。

vocabulary.entry: **megalodon** /ˈmeɡələdɒn/ n. 巨齿鲨（古生物专有名词）
vocabulary.example: Megalodon was a giant prehistoric shark.
vocabulary.translation: 巨齿鲨是一种巨大的史前鲨鱼。

vocabulary.entry: **pre-historic** /ˌpriː hɪˈstɒrɪk/ adj. 史前的（书面语）
vocabulary.example: Pre-historic cave paintings have been found in France.
vocabulary.translation: 在法国发现了史前洞穴壁画。

vocabulary.entry: **plentiful** /ˈplentɪfl/ adj. 丰富的，充足的（书面语）
vocabulary.example: Fresh water is plentiful in this region.
vocabulary.translation: 这个地区淡水充足。

vocabulary.entry: **species** /ˈspiːʃiːz/ n. 物种（单复数同形）
vocabulary.example: There are many species of birds in this forest.
vocabulary.translation: 这片森林里有许多种鸟类。

vocabulary.entry: **Carboniferous period** /ˌkɑːbəˈnɪfərəs ˈpɪəriəd/ n. 石炭纪（地质学术语）
vocabulary.example: The Carboniferous period was a time of vast coal-forming forests.
vocabulary.translation: 石炭纪是广阔的成煤森林时期。

vocabulary.entry: **oxygen level** /ˈɒksɪdʒən ˌlevl/ n. 氧气含量（固定表达）
vocabulary.example: High oxygen levels in the past allowed insects to grow larger.
vocabulary.translation: 过去的高氧气含量使昆虫能够长得更大。

vocabulary.entry: **insect** /ˈɪnsekt/ n. 昆虫
vocabulary.example: Bees, ants, and butterflies are all insects.
vocabulary.translation: 蜜蜂、蚂蚁和蝴蝶都是昆虫。

vocabulary.entry: **tracheal system** /trəˈkiːəl ˌsɪstəm/ n. 气管系统（昆虫学专业术语）
vocabulary.example: Insects breathe through their tracheal system.
vocabulary.translation: 昆虫通过气管系统呼吸。

vocabulary.entry: **tube** /tjuːb/ n. 管子，管道
vocabulary.example: The plant has tiny tubes that transport water.
vocabulary.translation: 这种植物有输送水分的小管。

vocabulary.entry: **enable** /ɪˈneɪbl/ v. 使能够，使成为可能（书面语）
vocabulary.example: The new software enables users to edit videos easily.
vocabulary.translation: 新软件使用户能够轻松编辑视频。

vocabulary.entry: **breathe** /briːð/ v. 呼吸
vocabulary.example: It's hard to breathe in this smoky room.
vocabulary.translation: 在这个烟雾弥漫的房间里很难呼吸。

vocabulary.entry: **picture** /ˈpɪktʃə(r)/ v. 想象，描绘
vocabulary.example: Can you picture yourself living in another country?
vocabulary.translation: 你能想象自己生活在另一个国家吗？

sentences.chinese: 阿根廷巨鸟是已发现的最大的飞鸟。

sentences.chinese: 它生活在大约600万年前，翼展达七米，是当今地球上最大的鸟类之一安第斯神鹰的两倍多。

sentences.english: And we can't forget the giant shark that roamed the oceans, megalodon.
sentences.chinese: 我们也不能忘记在海洋中漫游的巨齿鲨。

sentences.chinese: 想象一下在海里游泳时遇到一条18米长的鲨鱼！

sentences.chinese: 它们大约在260万年前灭绝了。

sentences.chinese: 那么，为什么史前动物如此巨大呢？

One is that, in the past, resources were more plentiful, so species were able to grow larger because they could eat more.
sentences.chinese: 其一是过去资源更丰富，所以物种能够长得更大，因为它们可以吃得更多。

sentences.english: Scientists also believe that during certain periods of history, such as in the Carboniferous period, there were higher oxygen levels on Earth.
sentences.chinese: 科学家还认为，在地球的某些历史时期，比如石炭纪，氧气含量更高。

sentences.english: At this time, some insects grew to the size of cars because of better oxygen delivery in their tracheal system, the network of tubes that enable insects to breathe.
sentences.chinese: 当时，由于气管系统（使昆虫能够呼吸的管状网络）能更好地输送氧气，一些昆虫长到了汽车那么大。

sentences.english: Can you picture animals being so huge today?
sentences.chinese: 你能想象今天的动物也如此巨大吗？
